sources.note: Only an areal remark, sec. 3.2 p. 115: 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables' (about Flores languages generally). Lamatuka [lmq] appears only in the Lamaholot classification tree (p. 166, East Lamaholot with Lewo Eleng [lwe]), in comparative lexical tables, and in fn. 22 p. 137 (lexicostatistics from Keraf 1978:448). No Lamatuka-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Keraf, Gregorius. 1978. Daftar Kata Dasar. In Morfologi Dialek Lamalera, 406-447. Jakarta: Universitas Indonesia (also Ende: Arnoldus). Lamatuka 200-item wordlist as digitized in LexiRumah 3, lect lama1277-lamat.

sources.note: Participatory language-vitality survey of seven Lembata Lamaholot languages including Lamatuka (desa Lamatuka, EGIDS 6a -> 6b). Sociolinguistic only; nothing on phonology or stress. Its reference list names no phonological description of Lamatuka (only Keraf 1978, Fricke 2017/2019).

sources.citation: Fricke, Hanna L.A. 2019. Traces of language contact: The Flores-Lembata languages in eastern Indonesia. LOT Dissertation Series 544. Utrecht: LOT (Leiden PhD).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.2.5 (pp. 49-50) gives a stress rule (penultimate unless the penult has schwa, then ultimate) for Central Lembata, a Central Lamaholot variety coded ISO lvu (Kalikasa, Atadei district) -- not Lamatuka. Sec. 4.1.5 (p. 160): Eastern Lamaholot (varieties Lewoeleng and Lamatuka) 'remains largely undescribed'; the only materials are Keraf's (1978) two 200-item wordlists. Table 4.2 (p. 162) lists 'lmt lmq Lamatuka Keraf 1978b' under Eastern Lamaholot. No statement on Lamatuka stress anywhere in the text (a full-text search for stress/accent hits only CL).
